analysis: The supplied changes are documentation only. CHANGELOG.md is modified, and docs/provider/cli-reference.md changes the 'Last updated' stamp (2026-10-02 to 2026-10-05) and adds a paragraph. The paragraph says that for sandboxed foreground/local startup, TMPDIR selects the anonymous runtime metallib snapshot directory and is not forwarded to the background provider. It points to docs/reference/configuration.md#runtime-metallib-snapshots, which I was not shown. No executable code, wire protocol, authorization, encryption, billing or attestation logic changed in the supplied units. The changelog excerpts describe provider and coordinator behavior in prose only: SSD prefix-cache defaults (a 100 GiB ceiling limited to half the available space, per cache configuration), complete Qwen checkpoints, and operator-restricted network prefix caching. They do not show the underlying source, so I cannot confirm the changelog matches the code. T-041 in the canonical context still describes the SSD disk budget as available-disk/2 with no fixed ceiling and a 20 GiB fallback. The changelog's new 100 GiB ceiling is a documentation-level mismatch with that threat-model text. I treat it as a threat-model update item for any reviewer who sees the code change, not as a finding, because the changelog is not authoritative for behavior and no code was supplied. The changelog also describes provider-side prefix-cache scoping and the SSD tier (T-041, SEC-035), including complete-checkpoint binding to weights, runtime, and prompt contract. A code-level pass should verify these against SSDPrefixCache and the coordinator cache_route_keys code. The TMPDIR snapshot directory claim concerns provider process isolation (TB-003). The code that implements it was not supplied, so that behavior needs a source-level check. Nothing in this batch was analyzed beyond the visible text, and the other units in this PR may carry the code changes.
